subject: Logic
title: Risk vs Reward
description: A short lesson to help you apply Risk vs Reward.

hook.text: A guaranteed $500 or a 50% chance of $1,200? Most people grab the sure money—even though the gamble pays more.

buildup.text: Risk aversion means preferring a certain outcome over a gamble with higher expected value.

discovery.text: It's rational when the downside could hurt you badly. Losing your rent money is worse than missing a bonus.

twist.text: Strangely, people become risk-seeking when facing guaranteed losses—they'll gamble to avoid a sure loss.

climax.text: Your risk tolerance should match the stakes. Small bets, expected value. Life savings, protect the downside.

punchline.text: Big upside means nothing if the downside ends the game.

quiz.question: When is risk aversion rational?
options: When the potential loss could cause severe harm
